query: What product attributes are associated with higher satisfaction scores?

per_column.name: review_text_length
per_column.rationale: An external associational variable (review verbosity) that could relate to satisfaction, but as a raw character count it is extremely fine-grained with hundreds of near-singleton values; it must be binned before any meaningful segmentation/comparison can be drawn.

per_column.name: summary_length
per_column.rationale: Same issue: a continuous length count spread across many values. Associational in principle, but not directly interpretable as well-separated categories without bucketing.

per_column.name: exclamation_count
per_column.rationale: Discrete, low-cardinality, and interpretable (proxy for emotional intensity). Values concentrate on 0/1/2/3+, allowing clean grouping and comparison against satisfaction.

per_column.name: positive_words_count
per_column.rationale: Interpretable count with a small range (0-9), easily segmented. Plausibly associated with satisfaction, though it verges on tautology since positive language and high scores co-occur.

per_column.name: negative_words_count
per_column.rationale: Interpretable in concept, but the distribution is near-constant (89% zeros), so it offers very little variation to compare across satisfaction levels.

per_column.name: helpfulness_ratio
per_column.rationale: A genuinely external community-signal variable (helpful votes fraction) distinct from the review content; interpretable and groupable (0, 1, and fractions), enabling a meaningful relationship with satisfaction.

per_column.name: sentiment_score
per_column.rationale: This is effectively pos-minus-neg word count; a bare sentiment aggregate that is essentially a proxy/restatement of the satisfaction signal rather than an independent attribute to compare against.

per_column.name: review_quality
per_column.rationale: An opaque composite score with undefined derivation and arbitrary values (0.34/0.67); not interpretable as a segmentation and provides no transparent axis for exploration.

per_column.name: high_satisfaction
per_column.rationale: This is a binarized version of the focus variable itself, not an external attribute; it restates satisfaction and cannot serve as an independent predictor to compare against it.

judge.rationale: The set is dominated by mechanical text statistics. A few columns (exclamation_count, positive_words_count, helpfulness_ratio) are interpretable, low-cardinality external variables that support real segmentation against satisfaction, with helpfulness_ratio being the strongest genuinely independent attribute. However, high_satisfaction restates the focus, sentiment_score and positive_words_count edge toward tautology with the satisfaction signal, review_quality is opaque, negative_words_count is near-constant, and the two length columns are too fine-grained to segment without binning. As a whole it provides only moderate support for discovering interpretable relationships with the focus.
